title: 1952 AHSME Problem 11
statement: If \(y=f(x)=\dfrac{x+2}{x-1},\) then it is incorrect to say:

solutions.text:
The function is undefined at \(x=1\) because its denominator is zero there, so \(f(1)=0\) is false. The other statements hold: \(f(0)=-2,\) \(f(-2)=0,\) solving \(y=\frac{x+2}{x-1}\) gives \(x=\frac{y+2}{y-1},\) and this same formula shows that \(f\) is its own inverse.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Check the domain of the rational function before evaluating it
